title: Thousands March on Parliament as NEET Protests and Lathi Charges Mark Monsoon Session Opening
excerpt: Police used tear gas and batons against CJP protesters attempting to reach Parliament on the first day of the monsoon session, as opposition leaders forced repeated adjournments in both Houses over NEET irregularities and Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • 10,000 protesters marched towards Parliament on July 20, defying police orders.
  • Police used tear gas and batons; five Delhi Metro stations were closed.
  • Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha faced multiple adjournments over NEET issues.
  • CJP leaders met with Union Minister J.P. Nadda amid ongoing protests.
  • Activist Sonam Wangchuk set conditions to end his hunger strike from the hospital.

  • Thousands of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protesters attempted a 'Chalo Sansad' march from Jantar Mantar toward Parliament on July 20, the first day of the monsoon session, defying police prohibitory orders.
  • Security forces used tear gas, lathi charges and barricades against demonstrators; Delhi Metro shut five stations and internet services were cut near the protest site.
  • Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha saw repeated adjournments as opposition MPs, including SP's Dimple Yadav and Congress's Mallikarjun Kharge, demanded discussion on NEET irregularities and condemned police action against students.
  • CJP spokespersons met Union Minister J.P. Nadda for talks while hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk, hospitalised since July 18, offered conditions to end his 22-day fast.

Tens of thousands of student protesters clashed with police in central New Delhi on Monday as they attempted to march on Parliament, turning the opening of India's monsoon session into a day of standoffs on the streets and serial disruptions inside both Houses.

The Cockroach Janta Party's planned 'Chalo Sansad' march, timed for the first day of the July 20–August 13 session, brought an estimated 10,000 demonstrators to Jantar Mantar by dawn, according to Delhi's Deputy Commissioner of Police Sachin Sharma. Many had arrived overnight following a vigil called by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.

Parliament's Turbulent Opening
›Opposition MPs demanded discussions on NEET irregularities.
›Rajya Sabha adjourned for the entire day.
›Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi condemned police actions.
›CJP's movement has 22 million Instagram followers.
https://x.com/TheQuint/status/2079036938125000949

Tear Gas and Barricades in Central Delhi

Delhi Police had imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita across the New Delhi district and stated that no permission had been sought or granted for the march. Despite the ban, protesters pushed forward.

Around 11:25 am, demonstrators attempted to breach multi-layered barricades near Parliament Street, according to PTI. Security forces responded with tear gas near Shastri Bhawan and lathi charges near Parliament Street, with the All India Students' Association alleging that several of its activists were beaten. Delhi Police denied any use of force, stating the "protest is being handled professionally," even as ANI broadcast footage of officers using batons.

"The protest site has already run out of space and this can lead to an untoward situation."

— Sachin Sharma, Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, to Reuters

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation shut five stations including Rajiv Chowk and Janpath, stranding commuters. Internet services were also cut in the protest area, with telecom providers sending alerts citing "Government instructions."

Parliament Paralysed on Day One

Inside Parliament, both Houses were repeatedly adjourned as opposition members refused to allow proceedings until their demands were heard. The Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the entire day after Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge rose to speak on the NEET paper leak.

"Thousands of students have reached Jantar Mantar and they were lathi-charged. The government is trying to beat them down and suppress the issue."

— Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress President and Leader of Opposition, Rajya Sabha

The Lok Sabha was adjourned six times on its first day, with opposition MPs raising slogans over NEET irregularities, the alleged theft of Ram Temple donations and other issues. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra condemned the use of tear gas against students, saying, "They are our children."

Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav led a delegation of party lawmakers to Jantar Mantar to express solidarity with CJP protesters. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav compared the government's handling of the crisis to colonial-era British suppression. "When people sat in protest, the British actually listened to them," Yadav told reporters at Parliament.

AAP leaders Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh and former Delhi Chief Minister Atishi also joined protesters at the site, along with actor Shabana Azmi, advocate Prashant Bhushan and activist Yogendra Yadav.

Government Opens Talks as Wangchuk Sets Conditions

In a significant development, the government reached out to CJP for talks. Spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka met Union Minister J.P. Nadda at around noon, though no official statement emerged from the meeting.

"The government had reached out for talks in the morning. Our demands are clear. The youth have gathered in huge numbers," Das posted on X.

Separately, activist Sonam Wangchuk — who has been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28, and was forcibly moved to Safdarjung Hospital on July 18 — wrote a handwritten note from hospital outlining conditions to end his fast. He said he would break his strike if the government took responsibility for education system failures or if lawmakers assured him the issues would be raised during the session.

His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, filed an appeal in the Delhi High Court seeking to transfer him to a private hospital, which was taken up by a division bench on Monday afternoon.

What Comes Next

The monsoon session is scheduled to run through August 13 with 19 sittings planned. The government has listed seven bills for the session, including the Supreme Court (Amendment) Bill and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill. But the opposition has signalled it will not allow normal business until NEET and education accountability are discussed.

Meanwhile, the CJP movement — born from a satirical response to a Supreme Court justice's remark comparing unemployed youth to "cockroaches" — has grown into the largest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term. The movement's 22 million Instagram followers and the breadth of Monday's mobilisation suggest the pressure on the government is unlikely to ease soon.
image_caption: Security forces face off with protesters during a demonstration in Delhi. Thousands of Cockroach Janta Party supporters attempted to march from Jantar Mantar toward Parliament on Monday, clashing with police who deployed tear gas and lathi charges.
nri_angle: The NEET paper leak has directly affected thousands of Indian-origin medical aspirants worldwide who sat the exam, while the CJP movement's 22-million Instagram following includes significant diaspora participation.
